sheets.name: README
rows: Traceability view for one regulation-to-SHACL generation run.
Generation is frozen before RDF execution; no ship graph or hidden expected outcome is used here.
events.jsonl is append-only; CSV and Excel sheets are derived views.
Static validation passed and the semantic validator accepted the candidate.
No verified canonical term was available; the generator was not allowed to invent one.
Accepted shapes await the separate bulk evaluator.

sheets.name: RUNS
rows: The bow-form alternatives still impose buttockAngle and normalFrameAngle sh:minCount 1 in both branch node shapes, so sh:or makes both angle properties mandatory for every ship and contradicts the conditional applicability requirement. Remove those branch minCount constraints; retain the two SPARQL branch checks so a branch passes only when both angle operands are present and establish either the applicable condition (gamma > 0, gamma < 80, beta' > 10) or its complementary non-applicable condition. With neither or incomplete angle evidence, both branches must fail, preventing missing branch-selection evidence from passing. Preserve the existing canonical owners, paths, units, datatypes, controlled alternatives, and exact inclusive AR = 3.6 bounds.

rows: Do not use the free-standing bowFormApplicability boolean as the applicability gate: it is not a declared applicability term, and its false value lets invalid gamma/beta values pass. Encode the verified angle conditions directly for the applicable bow-form case, or require the applicability value to be deterministically entailed by those angles rather than independently supplied. Restrict assignedHullArea to the declared controlled alternatives otherIceStrengthenedArea and otherIceStrengthenedAreaValue; the current sh:in also permits unrelated bow/midbody/stern region individuals, including values outside the property's canonical hullAreaValue range. Preserve the required ship-to-hullAreaAssignment-to-hullAreaValue path and all declared operand constraints.

Do not impose buttockAngle and normalFrameAngle minCount and bounds on every ship: the requirement makes the design-force applicability conditional on a bow form. Encode the bow-form applicability branch using evidence deterministically entailed by the angle conditions, without using a free-standing bowFormApplicability boolean or allowing a missing branch selector to pass. Preserve the direct angle comparisons (>0, <80, and >10 degrees), all declared operand paths, units, and the ship-to-hullAreaAssignment-to-assignedHullArea controlled alternatives.

Repair the bow-form alternatives: SHACL SPARQL SELECT results are violations, but the applicable branch currently selects valid angle evidence and the non-applicable branch selects invalid evidence, so sh:or can accidentally pass both cases. Make the applicable branch pass only when gamma > 0, gamma < 80, and beta' > 10, and make the non-applicable branch pass only when the angle evidence demonstrates the complementary condition; do not allow a missing branch-selection evidence set to pass. Also avoid imposing buttockAngle and normalFrameAngle minCount on every ship through both alternatives: keep those requirements conditional while ensuring the selected branch has the required angle evidence. Preserve the ship-to-hullAreaAssignment-to-assignedHullArea path and the two declared controlled alternatives, all operand paths, datatypes, and units.

The bow-form alternatives still impose buttockAngle and normalFrameAngle sh:minCount 1 in both branch node shapes, so sh:or makes both angle properties mandatory for every ship and contradicts the conditional applicability requirement. Remove those branch minCount constraints; retain the two SPARQL branch checks so a branch passes only when both angle operands are present and establish either the applicable condition (gamma > 0, gamma < 80, beta' > 10) or its complementary non-applicable condition. With neither or incomplete angle evidence, both branches must fail, preventing missing branch-selection evidence from passing. Preserve the existing canonical owners, paths, units, datatypes, controlled alternatives, and exact inclusive AR = 3.6 bounds.
